newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sakakibara seeks yen stronger than 120/$ -- ex-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Sakakibara seeks yen stronger than 120/$ -- ex-MOF.

text.p: Eisuke Sakakibara, a key official of Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF), has in mind a yen rate slightly stronger than 120 yen to the dollar, a former MOF official told reporters on Thursday.
Tomomitsu Oba, former vice finance minister for international affairs, made the remarks to reporters after attending a financial seminar addressed by both himself and Sakakibara.
"I think Mr. Sakakibara has a slightly stronger yen in mind than what I think about exchange rates," Oba said. Oba said he himself considers a dollar/yen rate of 120 yen an appropriate level.

Bankers who attended the seminar quoted Sakakibara as saying that that he does not rule out a rise in Japan's interest rates in the medium term. They also quoted him as saying that an imminent rise in Japan's interest rates is unlikely.
